note: Held/slow ERP state, re-anchored on the 1st business day of each month (or when the real-yield master / SP500 normalized series publish a new vintage). Between anchors ONLY the daily real curve + norm_ey move.

sources.reals_5_10_20_30: Treasury Daily Par Real Yield Curve (5/7/10/20/30); 7y optional belly point
sources.nominal_1y: Treasury Daily Par Yield Curve, 1Y tenor
sources.one_year_real_rule: real_1y = nominal_1y - breakeven1y (breakeven held from the monthly master vintage)
sources.norm_ey_rule: norm_ey = 100 * normalized_X4 * cpi_factor / sp_close  (SP500 normalized earnings LEVEL / real price; price is daily)

corp_prem_derivation: Corrected 2026-08-12 (AEG-ERP-TASK6-BUILD-SPEC / James's follow-up instruction). Was a static 1.8 with no documented derivation and no visible tie to the decided design. Now = asfp.volsurface.floor_from_credit_grid(cg, wedge=0.50) on the live credit grid (outputs/market_credit_latest.csv, 2026-08-12 vintage): bond risk premium 0.52% (30y IG index spread 1.00%, less 0.18% expected loss [lgd=0.60 x hazard=0.30], less 0.30% liquidity haircut) plus 0.50% cost premium = 1.02% total. Matches the decided-design METHOD (corporate credit risk premium + cost premium, per AEG-ERP-Plateau-Presets-And-Glide-SPEC-2026-08-12.md); does not match its 1.26% EXAMPLE figure, which was a hand calc from HQM corporate yield less nominal Treasury on a different day -- a ~24bp difference in the credit-spread reading itself, not a methodology disagreement. VERIFIED NON-BINDING both before and after this change: June 2026's own implied erp_risk (3.384) and 2026-08-12's (3.422) both sit far above either 1.8 or 1.02, so this correction does not move any published number retroactively or on the day it landed -- it closes a latent risk (the wrong floor silently taking over in a future selloff), not an active one. Re-derive at each monthly re-anchor rather than holding this value indefinitely -- the live credit spread moves.
